newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Regulators aim for Asia surveillance group.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Regulators aim for Asia surveillance group.

text.p: Securities and exchange regulators meeting in Sydney said on Wednesday they hoped to establish an inter-market surveillance group to better monitor exchange trading in Asia.
The group would be fashioned on existing inter-market groups in North America and Europe and would aim to better ensure that a Sumitomo or Barings-like trading debacle would not be repeated in Asia.

"We need to establish a better forum to ensure Asia does not fall behind the rest of the world," David White, executive director of the Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission, told a news briefing.

Alan Cameron, chairman of the Australian Securities Commission, told Reuters it was still being decided whether to surveillance group should be limited to futures and derivatives activity, or extend to other aspects of exchange trading.
"That something we're still working out," he said.

The regulators acknowledged that the competitiveness of Asia's fast-growing number of exchanges would present problems in establishing an effective monitoring system. "The issue of confidentiality is quite a large obstacle," Cameron said.
But even with tighter controls, those using the exchanges must take more responsibility, Joseph Dial, commissioner of the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission said.
"The bottom line with regard to preventing such situations from recurring rests with the firms themselves," Dial said.
